title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is computing the dimension-0 pieces of the 'Teichmüller tower', i.e. the groupoids attached to maximally degenerate Mumford–Deligne curves, where every component is a pair of pants. These are the 'Lego' building blocks of the Esquisse d'un programme.

(1) The genus-0, three-point block. Let I be a 3-element set and S_0T_{0,I} the modular-dimension-0 Teichmüller groupoid. Its 'base points' form ω(I), a 2-element set: the two cyclic orders of I. Equivalently these are the two real half-planes (two hexagons) of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, which are exchanged by odd permutations. The group S_I^+ ≅ A_3 is the stabilizer of x ∈ ω(I).

The previous page computed π_1(S_0T_{0,I}, S_I; x), the fundamental group including the S_I-symmetry, as an extension
0 → Z^I → G(I) → S_I → 1.
It is obtained by pulling back 0 → Z →(×2) Z → Z/2 → 0 along sgn: S_I → μ_2 and pushing out along diag: Z → Z^I. Concretely, a transposition lifts to a 'half-twist' whose square is a product of boundary twists. This is the familiar relation (half-twist)^2 = twist of the pair against the twists of the two boundaries, i.e. the balancing axiom c^2 = θ_{V⊗W}(θ_V^{-1}⊗θ_W^{-1}).
- The extension is non-split: it is already non-split over a transposition.
- It splits canonically over S_I^+, via α ↦ (0, α).

This page first observes that the result does not depend on x. G(I) is defined canonically, without reference to a base point, so it is functorial in I. Hence Aut(I) = S_I acts on G(I) by transport of structure, compatibly with its actions on Z^I and on S_I (by conjugation). This action is not given by conjugation through a section, since none exists. Over S_I^+ it coincides with conjugation via the canonical splitting. This is the standard distinction between an action by functoriality and an inner action through a splitting.

(2) The general maximally degenerate graph. Let G be an 'MD' graph (dual graph of a Mumford–Deligne stable curve) of modular dimension 0: all vertices s ∈ S have genus 0 and three half-edges Â_s. Let G^b be the 'broken' graph, the disjoint union of the vertex stars G^b_s. Then
S_0T_{G^b} = ∏_s S_0T_{G^b_s} = ∏_s S_0T_{0,Â_s},
and S_0T_G is obtained from it by the homomorphism (20) Z^{half-edges} → Z^{edges}. Gluing two boundary curves identifies their two Dehn twists into one edge twist.

The base-point set is ε(G) = ε(G^b) = ∏_s ω(Â_s): a choice of cyclic orientation (hexagon / half-plane) at each pants, i.e. a ribbon structure on the trivalent graph. It is a torsor under r(G) = {±1}^S.

On the next page this becomes:
- E(G^b): the extension of r(G) by Z^{half-edges}, from (Z → Z → Z/2)^S pushed along Z^S → Z^{half-edges} (source map).
- S_0T_{G^b}: the transformation groupoid of E(G^b) acting on ε(G).
- E(G): the pushout along (20), with S_0T_G described likewise.

Purpose: an explicit presentation of the vertex groupoids (pants decompositions with twists, half-twists and orientation changes) of the Teichmüller tower, as needed for the Lego program of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The sign and normalisation of the half-twist relation depends on conventions (which projection Z^I → Z exhibits non-splitness), but the non-splitness claim is correct.
The page breaks off mid-construction; the formula for S_0T_G is completed on the next page.

ideas.what: Canonical, base-point-free extension G(I) of S_I by Z^I (orbifold π_1 of the 3-pointed genus-0 stratum with symmetries), non-split, split over A_3, with S_I acting by transport of structure rather than via a section

ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and Lego idea, but not this explicit computation

ideas.what: Describing the maximally degenerate stratum groupoid S_0T_G as obtained from the product over pants via the gluing map Z^{half-edges} → Z^{edges}
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller groupoid / Lego decomposition along pants decompositions; local π_1 near the deepest point of M̄_{g,n}

ideas.what: Base points ε(G) = ∏ ω(Â_s): choices of cyclic orientation (real half-plane/hexagon) at each trivalent vertex, a torsor under {±1}^S

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, explicit working-out of the dimension-0 Lego pieces of the Teichmüller tower. It covers the non-split half-twist extension, the base points given by cyclic orientations of the pants, and the pushout along the half-edge → edge gluing. All of this is now standard in the Teichmüller-groupoid and ribbon-category literature (Moore–Seiberg, Bakalov–Kirillov, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps). It is of historical interest as an early, precise formulation, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'groupe MD𝔈' is more likely 'graphe MD' (dual graph of a Mumford–Deligne curve), consistent with the notation G, G^b, S (vertices) and Â_s (half-edges).
The formula ε(G)=ε(G^b)=∏_{s∈S} ω(Â_s)/ε(G^b_s) is not a fraction: ε(G^b_s) is written under an underbrace, i.e. ε(G)=ε(G^b)=∏_{s∈S} ω(Â_s) with ω(Â_s) = ε(G^b_s).
(20) is presumably the map from twists on half-edges to twists on edges (Z^{\vec{Â}} → Z^{Â} in the notation of the next page), not Z^{Â} → Z^{Â}.
The phrase rendered 'par l'homo[?] du groupe d'op. extérieures' should read 'par l'homomorphisme du groupe d'opérations extérieures' ('dioph.' struck out).
'Il est assez [?] clair' is plausibly 'Il est assez clair' or 'Il est aussi clair'.
